records.description: For the declared infrared flow F(g), a fixed point g_* satisfies F_i(g_*)=0. Near it, d(delta g_i)/d ell=B_ij delta g_j+O(delta g^2), where B_ij=partial F_i/partial g_j at g_*. For an admitted eigen-direction with real eigenvalue y_a, its linear scaling field obeys u_a(ell)=exp(y_a ell)u_a(0). A nonredundant local operator of full fixed-point scaling dimension Delta_a coupled homogeneously in d dimensions has y_a=d-Delta_a. With ell increasing toward the infrared, y_a>0 is relevant, y_a<0 irrelevant and y_a=0 linearly marginal.
records.name: Local fixed-point scaling classification
openObligations: The displayed exponential applies to an eigen-direction in the linear regime. Operator mixing, non-diagonalizable blocks, redundant field redefinitions, symmetry restrictions and departures from the fixed-point neighborhood require explicit treatment; a complete diagonal basis is not assumed for arbitrary models. The displayed inequalities cover real eigenvalues; complex pairs need a real-part stability analysis outside this example.

Delta_a is the full scaling dimension, including anomalous contributions, not automatically the engineering dimension. A marginal direction needs higher-order flow or an additional exact argument to distinguish marginally relevant, marginally irrelevant and exactly marginal behavior.

An irrelevant perturbation decreases relative to the fixed point in this direction; its coefficient need not vanish at finite resolution or be negligible for every observable. Relevant does not mean more ontologically real, and marginal does not mean experimentally constant.

A fixed point, its attraction domain and any associated universality class must be established for the selected action, symmetries and approximation. This classification neither ensures that every flow reaches a fixed point nor proves universal autonomous higher-level laws.
